_readme: Which answers are a bot wall's challenge page (#480). Read by tests/test_bot_walls.py
markers: the defence names and the needles each is recognised by in the body: its first
body_prefix_bytes bytes, decoded as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced, ASCII-lowercased.
header_markers: the header names, lowercase, a defence sends only with a challenge;
compared whole with each ASCII-lowercased header name, values unread. Header values are
never searched: a defence's cookie, a CDN's Server value or a CSP naming a captcha comes
with ordinary answers too. Every platform's tables must equal these. gone_statuses:
never challenged. cloudflare_refusal_statuses: with a Server header that, trimmed of
spaces and tabs only and ASCII-lowercased, is 'cloudflare', a challenge whatever the
page says. A body beginning %PDF is never challenged. cases: body_padding_bytes spaces
are put before the body; body_base64, when present, is the body's bytes in place of
body (for bytes that are not UTF-8). expected: the sorted defence names; empty means
not challenged. Rules: doc/cross_platform/fulltext_retrieval.md, 'A challenged PDF
(#480)'. Sources: doc/developer/unpaywall_pdf_survey/; the Akamai and Cloudflare
managed-challenge bodies are live pages fetched 2026-10-13. Add a row here, not a test

anubis: making sure you're not a bot
